material.acceptance_criteria: Within every group, the gap between siblings is smaller than the gap between separate groups: the .w-box.row item gap is below the .w-root panel gap, and the .w-panel>h4 title-to-first-child gap is no larger than the gap between that panel's sibling children. Static: the gap and margin values at widgets.js:26-31 and 46 satisfy that order.
material.description: Surface: js/client/widgets.js (STYLE block; buildNode panel branch). Principle: Gestalt proximity (Wertheimer, Koffka, Köhler). Two spacing values place group-internal gaps above the gap between separate groups. (a) .w-box.row sets gap:6px (widgets.js:31) between sibling items of one row, while .w-root sets gap:4px between sibling panels (widgets.js:26), so two buttons in one row sit farther apart than two stacked panels. (b) buildNode appends the h4 title as the first child of section.w-panel (widgets.js:141-142). .w-panel has a flex gap of 4px (widgets.js:28) and .w-panel>h4 has margin-bottom 4px (widgets.js:29), so the title sits 8px above its first child while the panel's own children sit 4px apart. Panels stay closed by their 1px border, so this weakens grouping rather than clipping anything. Surface: js/client/hud.js asserts no cause; this row is a CSS finding in widgets.js.
material.subject: Panel spacing inverts the proximity hierarchy: row items sit farther apart than separate panels, and a panel title floats away from its content
